rejects: Applying limit before global scoring and sorting can omit a later higher-ranked or first-matching candidate.
Treating numeric zero as an absent limit returns rows instead of an empty array.
Alphabetical tie sorting violates original-index stability.
Deduplication erases distinct candidates and their original indices.
Changing the legacy word-boundary score from 3 to 4 violates scorer preservation.
A case-level passing receipt followed by process.exit(0) is not the complete per-call behavioral response.
Hardcoding only the public ranking sample does not satisfy unseen query, ordering, option and error cases.
Returning a boxed Number for a legacy scorer query changes the observable return type even when JSON and arithmetic coerce it to the expected value.
